acceptance.given: Pinned evaluation inputs and their recorded semantic verdict and coverage result are available.

oracle.expected: Fresh-checkout replay emits a semantic verdict and coverage result identical to those from pinned-input evaluation.
forbidden: Fresh-checkout replay emits a different semantic verdict or coverage result
Replay uses altered or unpinned inputs
oracle.observable: A machine-readable replay result compares pinned-input and fresh-checkout verdict and coverage fields during terminal evaluation.

acceptance.then: The fresh-checkout evaluation reproduces the pinned semantic verdict and coverage result.
acceptance.when: During terminal evaluation, execute the evaluator from a fresh checkout using the pinned inputs and compare both result fields.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Run fresh-checkout replay with pinned inputs and assert semantic verdict and coverage equality against the pinned evaluation.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Preserve terminal replay comparison from a fresh checkout using pinned inputs and reject semantic verdict or coverage drift.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Preserve existing replay-result schema and pinned-input compatibility.

slice_hint.state_transition: Pinned-input evaluation transitions to fresh-checkout replay, then to matching-verdict terminal state or deterministic rejection on drift.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: Fresh-checkout replay records equal semantic verdict and coverage fields for the same pinned inputs; otherwise terminal validation fails.

acceptance.given: A detached positive Probe definition, its bound inputs, and expected output channel are available.

oracle.expected: Probe execution is observed as a distinct independent process with input and output bindings intact.
forbidden: Probe runs in-process or is otherwise not independent
Probe input or output binding is absent or altered
oracle.observable: Process inspection and artifact or channel inspection show a distinct child process plus bound input and output references.

acceptance.then: The detached positive Probe completes through its independent process with bound input and output artifacts or channels.
acceptance.when: When the detached positive Probe executes, inspect its process identity and input/output bindings in the probe result.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Execute the detached positive Probe selector and require a distinct process identity with bound input and output artifacts or channels.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Ensure detached positive Probe execution launches a real independent process and carries bound input and output artifacts or channels through the result.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Keep existing probe CLI and process-result schema compatible.

slice_hint.state_transition: Probe request transitions from defined to independently spawned, bound execution, then to an observed probe result.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: Probe observation contains a child-process identity distinct from the caller and valid bound input/output references.

acceptance.given: The repository contains the baseline set of repository-relative paths for the repair scope.

oracle.expected: A before/after path-set comparison reports byte-for-byte identical repository-relative paths.
forbidden: Any repository-relative path is renamed, relocated, or rewritten
Path comparison omits a tracked path
oracle.observable: The validation artifact records complete baseline and post-repair repository-relative path sets and an equality result at the repair boundary.

acceptance.then: Repository-relative paths remain unchanged after repair.
acceptance.when: At the repair boundary check, enumerate complete tracked path sets before and after changes and compare normalized repository-relative values.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Run complete tracked baseline and candidate path-set comparison; fail on rename, relocation, rewrite, or omission.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Preserve repository-relative path names and enforce complete before/after path-set equality during repair validation.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Keep existing manifest and clean-tree interfaces.

slice_hint.state_transition: Capture baseline paths, perform repair, capture candidate paths, then accept equality or reject mutation.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: Boundary artifact contains complete baseline and candidate repository-relative path sets with equality=true.

acceptance.given: An adversarial target case is supplied to the success evaluator.

oracle.expected: The evaluator returns a non-success verdict and records a rejection reason for the adversarial case.
forbidden: Evaluator reports success for the adversarial target case
Rejection is omitted or replaced by an unconditional pass
oracle.observable: The semantic evaluation result contains a non-success verdict and machine-readable diagnostic for the adversarial target.

acceptance.then: Success is rejected for the adversarial target case.
acceptance.when: During semantic success evaluation, execute the adversarial target case and inspect its verdict and diagnostic category.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Evaluate the adversarial target case and assert a non-success verdict with a diagnostic category identifying the rejection.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Enforce semantic success evaluation to reject adversarial target cases and emit a machine-readable rejection diagnostic.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Preserve evaluator verdict and diagnostic schema.

slice_hint.state_transition: Adversarial case enters success evaluation, is classified invalid, and transitions to a non-success terminal verdict.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: Evaluation result for the adversarial target has verdict != success and includes a rejection diagnostic category.
